newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natgas prices strong in busy trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices strong in busy trade.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices held their recent strength in brisk Wednesday trade as gas demand for California electicity generation continued and domestic utilities bought in the Alberta market, trading sources said.
Gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was talked at about C$1.57 per gigajoule, virtually unchanged from last week. December AECO gas was quoted at C$1.575.
"All the winter months are strong," said a Calgary-based marketer. "Utilities have been hanging onto storage and they've been stepping into the day market a bit."

However, with some smaller Alberta gas plants expected back in service over the next few days after outages, more supply will be available, leading to the possibility of weaker prices by the weekend, the marketer said.

At the borders, Gas at Sumas, Washington was quoted in a wide range of US$2.20-2.23 per million British thermal units. Traders said a curtailment of interruptible service on Westcoast Energy's mainline was adding to the general tightness of British Columbia supply.

Forecast cooler temperatures in eastern Canada and the U.S. Northeast, as well as a jump in NYMEX and U.S. Gulf Coast prices, led to a five to 10 cent jump on the day for gas in southern Ontario points Dawn and Niagara. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
